description:
Workspace-wide clippy::pedantic doc-lint sweep. Three lint families, one coordinated commit per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' propagation rule (start at jmap-mail-server canonical, propagate to all extension-server siblings + foundation jmap-server in same pass).

## Lint families (per JMAP-x2gd.56 survey on chat-server alone)

- **clippy::doc_markdown** (item in documentation is missing backticks): 156 sites in chat-server. Type names, method names, crate names mentioned in doc-comments without backtick quoting. Renders as English text in cargo doc instead of as linked identifiers.

- **clippy::missing_errors_doc** (pub fn returning Result without '# Errors' section): 49 sites in chat-server. Downstream kit consumers want to know what each error variant means.

- **clippy::missing_panics_doc** (pub fn that may panic without '# Panics' section): 11 sites in chat-server. Critical for consumers — MemoryBackend.lock().unwrap() and .expect() sites need documented panic preconditions.

## Workspace scope estimate

- Foundation: jmap-types, jmap-server, jmap-mime, jmap-cid-types — probably 100-200 sites total.
- Type crates (mail, chat, calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing, metadata, jscalendar, jscontact) — probably 200-400 sites total.
- Server crates (8 extension-server crates + jmap-server foundation) — probably 800-1500 sites total.
- Client crates (base-client + 8 extension clients) — probably 100-200 sites total.

Workspace total likely 1500-2500 sites.

## Fix shape

1. **doc_markdown (mechanical, most automatable):** wrap type/method/crate names in backticks. Some sites require judgment to distinguish identifier-mentioned-as-identifier from identifier-mentioned-as-English-word (e.g. 'a Future' vs '`Future<...>`').

2. **missing_errors_doc (substantive):** for each pub fn returning Result, add a '# Errors' section enumerating each error variant the fn can return. Many sites have multiple error variants the writer needs to identify from the function body.

3. **missing_panics_doc (substantive, highest value):** for each pub fn that may panic, add a '# Panics' section. MemoryBackend's std::sync::Mutex::lock().unwrap() sites all panic on mutex poisoning if a previous holder panicked. Other .expect() sites need per-site analysis.

## Canonical-template propagation

Per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates':
- Foundation jmap-server first (jmap-mail-server depends on it).
- jmap-mail-server canonical for extension-server family.
- Propagate to chat-server, calendars-server, tasks-server, contacts-server, filenode-server, sharing-server, metadata-server in same pass.
- Same for foundation/extension type crates and client crates per their families.

## Why not piecemeal

JMAP-x2gd.56's own framing: 'Three lints; one sweep PR; one bead so the work shows up on a single sprint.' Doing one crate at a time would generate 30+ crate-scoped beads where each is doc-only churn that hides the next legitimate finding. A single coordinated sweep is the efficient form.

## Priority

P3 because:
- Pre-publish polish; the workspace's RUSTDOCFLAGS=--cfg docsrs -D warnings gate doesn't yet check pedantic doc lints.
- Reviewers DO read rustdoc, unbacktick'd identifiers look amateurish in a published API.
- The missing_panics_doc gap is the only one with safety/correctness implications (consumers need panic preconditions); could be split out as a higher-priority subset if desired.

title: Workspace-wide rustdoc polish sweep: clippy::pedantic doc-markdown + missing-errors + missing-panics (~1500-2500 sites)
